title: Pakistan Lowers Petrol and Diesel Prices
summary: The Pakistani government has announced a cut in domestic fuel rates, reducing the prices of petrol and high-speed diesel.
paragraphs: The federal government has reduced petroleum prices, marking another downward revision. Dawn and The Express Tribune reported that the price of petrol has been slashed by Rs8 per litre, while high-speed diesel has decreased by Rs7 per litre. Aaj News noted that this represents the sixth straight time the government has reduced petrol and diesel rates.

Following the revision, petrol is now priced at Rs338 per litre and diesel costs Rs371 per litre, according to Samaa and The Express Tribune. The new rates take effect under a daily price mechanism for Nov 11, The Express Tribune reported, while ARY News confirmed that the cuts came as the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority issued a new notification.

title: US and Iran Exchange Conflicting Signals on War and Negotiations
summary: Donald Trump claimed military action against Iran is largely over, while Iranian officials dismissed reports of bilateral talks as fabrication.
paragraphs: United States President Donald Trump stated that the war with Iran is effectively over and described additional strikes as quite unlikely, according to Euronews and BBC News. Speaking following discussions with Qatar's prime minister, Trump maintained that the United States remains locked and loaded should circumstances alter, while CNBC quoted him noting that Iran is militarily spent after losing its navy and enduring rampant inflation.

However, Iranian officials rejected assertions that diplomatic discussions are underway. Euronews reported that Iranian security chief Mohsen Rezaei accused Washington of producing fake news concerning imaginary negotiations. This comes amid wider diplomatic maneuvering, with Al Jazeera noting that Trump perceived positive momentum toward concluding the conflict following a Qatari ceasefire initiative.

title: France Accuses Iran of Cyberattacks on Supermarket Refrigerators
summary: French officials have directly blamed an Iranian Revolutionary Guard cyber unit for widespread October attacks targeting commercial cooling systems.
paragraphs: The French government has publicly accused the cyber unit of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps of conducting an unprecedented cyber campaign against supermarket refrigeration units, according to CNBC and France 24. The October sabotage operations caused millions of euros in damage across hundreds of retail stores, CNBC reported.

French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot confirmed the findings and stated that France will pursue coordinated European retaliatory measures and sanctions against Tehran, according to France 24 and Al Jazeera. The incident was also acknowledged in reporting by NHK World.

title: Deadly Industrial Blast Hits Turkish Steel Plant
summary: An industrial explosion at a steel factory in western Turkey has killed at least 16 people after a crane collapsed into a furnace.
paragraphs: A major explosion took place at a steel factory near Izmir in western Turkey, according to Al Jazeera and BBC News. BBC News identified the facility as the Habas Demir Celik plant in Aliaga.

Casualty counts varied slightly across reports. Al Jazeera and DW reported that at least 16 people died, citing an announcement by President Recep Tayyip Erdogan following a cabinet meeting. Euronews reported that at least 17 individuals were killed and 13 others were injured. According to Euronews and Al Jazeera, the disaster was triggered when a crane carrying a boiler collapsed into an industrial furnace.

title: Pope Leo XIV Warns Against Austerity During Argentina Visit
summary: During a pastoral trip to Argentina, Pope Leo XIV voiced concerns over government welfare cuts led by President Javier Milei.
paragraphs: Pope Leo XIV conducted a major mass in Buenos Aires that drew an estimated 2.5 million attendees, making it his largest gathering yet, according to DW. The pontiff's appearance comes in the midst of a 12-day tour across South America, Euronews reported.

During his trip, the Pope visited the Cottolengo Don Orione in Claypole, a facility supporting over 400 individuals, Euronews reported. Amid cuts enacted by President Javier Milei affecting disability care and broader social programs, DW and Euronews noted that the Pope urged the protection of society's most vulnerable populations, asserting that national progress should be measured by the treatment of those with the greatest needs.

title: Controversy Surrounds Russia's Return to Junior Ice Hockey Championship
summary: Norway has reportedly been removed from the upcoming World Juniors tournament to accommodate the return of Russia, sparking international debate and a boycott.
paragraphs: Norway stated that it has been kicked out of the upcoming major ice hockey tournament to create room for Russia, DW reported. Euronews detailed that the International Ice Hockey Federation moved Norway, which is ranked 10th, down to Division 1A to free up a spot for Russia at the event in Alberta. This adjustment followed an order from the Court of Arbitration for Sport requiring the reinstatement of Russian teams.

However, Euronews reported that the alteration is not yet officially confirmed, and Russia currently has no guarantee of receiving Canadian visas. Amid the ongoing dispute over Russia's reintroduction to global hockey, Switzerland has decided to join a boycott, according to DW.
